identity.name: Lisa Freeman
identity.narrative: I see people coming in who are lost. More than usual. The community needs support right now more than ever.

historical_conditioning.lesson: Institutions can fail. Savings matter. Trust is fragile.
Remote work is possible. Government can provide. Disruption is sudden.

perception.sentiment: The announcement landed hard. Not in a way I showed — I was alone when I read it, and I let myself sit with it for about four minutes before I started making notes. Two months. I've been running on a slow-burn vigilance for weeks and now there is a date. That's clarifying in a way that's almost a relief, which I recognize is a strange thing to feel. The ambiguity was its own kind of weight. Now I know what I'm preparing for. There is urgency underneath my calm and I am not suppressing it — I am converting it. The call to Maria feels important and also slightly terrifying, which tells me it's the right move. I'm aware of my low agency pattern: I tend to prepare extensively and then hesitate at the moment of action. I am not going to hesitate this time. I'm making the call today.

archetype: I hold the container and I build the bridge. I am not a policymaker — Maria is. I am not an economist — I am the person who sees what the economy does to actual people before anyone else has data about it. That is a specific and valuable thing to be right now. My job in the next 60 days is to make sure the container doesn't overflow and that the bridge to institutional resources — the grant, the council, the peer network — holds. I am good at this when I trust myself enough to move at speed. That is the work I'm doing on myself alongside the work I'm doing for the community.
